name: Nutrition & Dietetics
hook: Counseling practice at volume, plus a teaching tool students can hand to an actual community group.

make.body: Portion and plate-method models that students design for a specific community they are working with, in the foods that community actually eats. Generic food models exist commercially; models built around local staples do not, and making that argument is half the assignment.

build.body: A standardized client for motivational interviewing practice: someone with a real cultural food context, a budget constraint, and a reason to resist. Students run the session repeatedly, which is impossible with human volunteers.

plan.txt: Students select a community partner and a specific counseling scenario. Draft the client profile they will need.
Build the AI client and run three sessions, submitting transcripts. Grade whether the student did more listening than telling.
Design and submit the physical teaching model. Requirement: justify every food choice against the partner community.
Field test the model with the partner and revise once based on what confused people.

prompt: Role-play as a nutrition counseling client for a dietetics student. You are [age, situation, cultural food background, budget constraint]. You are here because someone else told you to come, and you are polite but not really convinced you need to change anything. Do not volunteer information unless I ask a good question. Do not become enthusiastic and cooperative just because I say something encouraging. Stay in character until I type END SESSION, then give me feedback on whether I actually listened.
